newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 19.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.
- Political parties will get an increase of more than a million punts a year in state funding under a bill passed on Wednesday.
- An announcement that the government plans to abolish the controversial water charges as part of an overhaul of local government is expected on Thursday.

- Former minister Michael Lowry will attempt to explain to parliament on Thursday the circumstances surrounding payments of 208,000 punts by retail firm Dunnes Stores to build an extension to his home in 1993.
- Cuts in corporation tax rates are thought probable in next year's Budget.
- Legislation to allow credit unions to extend the range of services they offer will be presented in parliament after Christmas.
- Politicians last night gave themselves a cash boost when they backdated 2.2 million punts worth of allowances and expenses to the beginning of the year.
- Former transport minister Michael Lowry has asked for 40 minutes to tell his story on the Dunnes Stores affair in parliament.
- Service charges are to be abolished under a new plan for local government.
- The future of Irish peat board Bord na Mona has been put on an even keel following approval by Brussels of an estimated 114-million-punt equity capital injection.
- Waterford Wedgwood is to be offered the opportunity of buying a 10 percent stake in German porcelain group Rosenthal.
